rationale: This is the archived "Post-Deleveraging Sales Value" mechanism with only normalization swaps (IND_RANK→TS_RANK, RANK→IND_ZSCORE), so it is a largely cosmetic rescaling of a construct that already failed on alpha, and because TS_RANK is strictly positive the signal's sign is driven almost entirely by the deleveraging z-score leg rather than by any genuine interaction.

The lct/lt maturity-concentration level is a genuinely new conditioning variable in this archive (prior attempts used changes in dlc/lt or netted short-term debt), the expected negative sign is consistent with the expression, though the value leg again only scales magnitude so the test is close to a standalone debt-maturity-structure signal.

The conditioning term Δ(act−che) minus the increase in current liabilities, scaled by assets, is essentially the classic working-capital accrual measure, so despite the one-sided MAX twist this is close to a rediscovery of the Sloan accrual anomaly interacted with book-to-market.

This differs from the archived "Earnings-Instability Value Trap" only by lengthening the volatility window from 3 to 5 and switching the value leg's normalization, which is a parameter tweak rather than a substantively different mechanism addressing why the alpha was wrongly signed.

A trend in a coverage-of-current-liabilities ratio interacted with cheapness has already been tested twice in this archive (Cash-Runway Trend Value, Downside Cash-Coverage Value) with weak results, and substituting EBITDA for cash in the numerator is a cosmetic variant of the same failed family.

This wraps the archived "Uncovered Maturity Residual Yield" expression verbatim in a TS_RANK, which is a pure renormalization rather than a new mechanism, and the claim that it isolates "distress resolution" mispricing is not supported by anything the expression actually computes.
